name: Aztecs
hook: A Mesoamerican empire of gold, gods and human sacrifice, undone by Cortés in two years.

facts.label: Tenochtitlan
facts.statement: Tenochtitlan was the Aztec capital, built on an island in Lake Texcoco on the site of modern Mexico City; its sister city was Tlatelolco.

facts.label: Hernán Cortés
facts.statement: Hernán Cortés sailed from Cuba in 1519 and toppled the Aztec Empire for Spain; Doña Marina served as his interpreter and mistress.

facts.label: Montezuma II
facts.statement: Montezuma II was the Aztec emperor when Cortés arrived in 1519; he died in 1520, and the empire fell in 1521 when Cuauhtémoc was captured.

facts.label: Quetzalcoatl
facts.statement: Quetzalcoatl was the feathered-serpent wind god; the story that the Aztecs mistook Cortés for him is a later legend, not contemporary fact.

facts.label: Huitzilopochtli
facts.statement: Huitzilopochtli was the Aztec god of war and the sun, brother of Quetzalcoatl; priests offered human sacrifices to him atop pyramid temples.

facts.label: Nahuatl
facts.statement: Nahuatl was the Aztec language; Popocatépetl, the volcano whose name means "smoking mountain," is a Nahuatl word.

facts.label: Aztec gifts
facts.statement: The Aztecs gave the world chocolate and vanilla; they prized turquoise, and a double-headed serpent mosaic of it is an icon of their art.
